name: Douglas-Charles Airport
before:
Dominica's main airport, on the north east coast 2 miles from Marigot, and one of only two on the island. The other is Canefield, near Roseau.

Distances matter here more than the size of the airport. Portsmouth, the island's second town, is about an hour away by road, so build a real transfer into any itinerary.

The terminal is small and straightforward: ten check in counters and two ground level gates, with no air bridges. Gate 1 is used by American and American Eagle, and Gate 2 by United on Saturdays.

The addition worth mentioning to a client is the Executive Lounge, which is open to both arriving and departing passengers. It includes seating, Wi-Fi, complimentary food and drink, cultural exhibits, private rest rooms and, usefully, assistance through immigration and customs, baggage help and taxi arrangements.

The airport was formerly called Melville Hall, a name still in circulation.
after:
Dominica's main airport, on the north east side of the island near Marigot, and one of only two on Dominica. The other is Canefield, near Roseau.

Distances matter here more than the size of the airport. Roseau, the capital, is about an hour away by road, so build a real transfer into any itinerary.

American Airlines flies here direct from Miami.

The feature worth mentioning to a client is the Executive Lounge, open to departing passengers, with Wi-Fi and drinks.

Its former name, Melville Hall, is still in circulation.

claims.claim: ten check-in counters, two ground-level gates, no air bridges
claims.wasBefore: The terminal is small and straightforward: ten check in counters and two ground level gates, with no air bridges.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and Wikipedia contradicts itself (two ground-level gates in one section, a Gate 3 for United in the next). Neither the operator nor the tourism authority gives counts; the tourism authority calls the terminal updated.

claims.claim: Gate 1 American and American Eagle; Gate 2 United on Saturdays
claims.wasBefore: Gate 1 is used by American and American Eagle, and Gate 2 by United on Saturdays.
claims.why: Gate assignments rest on Wikipedia alone (and it gives United Gate 2 in one place and Gate 3 in another). United's Newark service also rests on Wikipedia alone here: the tourism authority lists United only among airlines for connections, and the operator's press page lists nothing. American's Miami service is kept (see above).

claims.claim: Executive Lounge open to arriving passengers
claims.wasBefore: The addition worth mentioning to a client is the Executive Lounge, which is open to both arriving and departing passengers.
claims.why: Arrival access rests on Wikipedia alone; the lounge's own listing admits passengers with a same-day boarding pass. Softened to departing passengers (see above).

claims.claim: lounge includes seating, food, cultural exhibits, private rest rooms, immigration and customs assistance, baggage help, taxi arrangements
claims.wasBefore: It includes seating, Wi-Fi, complimentary food and drink, cultural exhibits, private rest rooms and, usefully, assistance through immigration and customs, baggage help and taxi arrangements.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, apart from the Wi-Fi and drinks, which the lounge's listing confirms and the new text keeps.

claims.claim: a new international airport is being built nearby
claims.why: Held back: Dominica's first international airport has been under construction at Wesley, a few kilometres north, since mobilisation in June 2023 (the development company; OurAirports lists the site). No opening date is published, and the old text said nothing that it replaces. When it opens, 'one of only two' will change.
